intro: Checking in, asking about breakfast and services, reporting problems and checking out. You speak to reception staff with *Sie*. The same phrases work in a *Pension*, a hostel or a holiday flat.

phrases.usage: The first sentence at reception; add your name: *... auf den Namen Keller.* Staff then usually say *Herzlich willkommen! Darf ich Ihren Ausweis sehen?*
phrases.grammar: Perfekt with *haben*. Verbs in *-ieren* form the Partizip II without *ge-*: *reserviert*. *das Zimmer* is neuter → Akkusativ *ein Zimmer*.

alternatives.de: Guten Tag, ich habe bei Ihnen ein Zimmer gebucht.
alternatives.en: Hello, I booked a room with you.

alternatives.de: Ich habe eine Buchung für zwei Nächte.
alternatives.en: I have a booking for two nights.

phrases.usage: Say it at reception or on the phone when you book. The other types are *Doppelzimmer* (double) and *Zweibettzimmer* (twin). The next question is usually *Für wie viele Nächte?*
phrases.grammar: *möchte* can be used without an infinitive when the object is clear; it takes the Akkusativ. *das Einzelzimmer* is neuter because the last part is *das Zimmer* → *ein*.

alternatives.en: I'd like a single room.
A single room, please.

phrases.usage: The receptionist asks this when you book. Answer *Mit Frühstück, bitte.* or *Ohne, danke.*
phrases.grammar: *mit* + Dativ, *ohne* + Akkusativ. At the end *ohne* stands alone because the noun is not repeated. *das Frühstück* has no article here (general meal).

alternatives.en: Would you like to book with breakfast?
Is breakfast included?

phrases.usage: Ask at check-in. The answer is *Von 7 bis 10 Uhr im Erdgeschoss.* or *im Restaurant*.
phrases.grammar: *es gibt* + Akkusativ ('there is'); *es* is impersonal and never changes. *wann* asks for the time.

alternatives.en: From what time is breakfast served?
Until when can you have breakfast?

phrases.usage: Ask at reception or in a large building. In Switzerland and Austria the usual word is *der Lift*.
phrases.grammar: *der Aufzug* is masculine (from *aufziehen*, no suffix → masculine). Nominativ subject.

alternatives.en: Where is the lift?
Is there an elevator here?

phrases.de: Mein Zimmer ist im dritten Stock.
phrases.en: My room is on the third floor.
phrases.usage: Floors are counted from the *Erdgeschoss* (ground floor), so *im dritten Stock* is three floors above the ground floor: British 'third floor', American 'fourth floor'.
phrases.grammar: *im* = *in dem* (Dativ, position). *der Stock* is masculine → *dem*. The ordinal after *dem* takes the weak ending **-en**: im dritt**en** Stock.

alternatives.de: Mein Zimmer ist in der dritten Etage.
alternatives.en: My room is on the third floor.

phrases.correction: The legacy text *Das Wifi-Passwort, bitte.* used *Wifi*. The standard German word in all three countries is *WLAN*, so the phrase now teaches *das WLAN-Passwort*.
phrases.usage: The standard German word is *WLAN* (spoken 'weh-lahn'), in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Signs often show the English *WiFi*, and in Switzerland people also say *Wifi* in speech. The password is often on the key card holder.
phrases.grammar: Akkusativ with the verb left out (*Geben Sie mir ...*). In a compound whose first part is an abbreviation, a hyphen is used: *das WLAN-Passwort*. *das Passwort* is neuter.

alternatives.en: What is the Wi-Fi password?
Is there Wi-Fi here?

phrases.de: Können Sie mir den Schlüssel geben?
phrases.en: Can you give me the key?
phrases.usage: Ask at reception when you come back to the hotel. Give your room number: *Zimmer 304.* Many hotels use key cards (*die Schlüsselkarte*).
phrases.grammar: *geben* takes a Dativ person (*mir*) and an Akkusativ thing (*den Schlüssel*); *der Schlüssel* is masculine → *den*. The infinitive *geben* is at the end.

alternatives.en: Can I have my key?

alternatives.de: Ich hätte gern den Schlüssel für Zimmer 304.
alternatives.en: I'd like the key for room 304.

phrases.en: When do I have to check out?
phrases.usage: Ask at check-in. The answer is *Bis 11 Uhr.* If you need more time, ask *Kann ich auch später auschecken?*
phrases.grammar: *auschecken* is an English loan used like a separable verb: *Ich checke um zehn aus.*, Partizip II *ausgecheckt*. After *muss* it stays together at the end.

alternatives.de: Bis wann muss ich das Zimmer räumen?
alternatives.en: By what time do I have to vacate the room?
Can I check out later?

phrases.usage: Ask after check-out when your train leaves later. The answer is *Ja, natürlich, Sie können es hier lassen.*
phrases.grammar: *aufbewahren* is separable (*Wir bewahren es auf.*, Partizip *aufbewahrt*). *das Gepäck* is neuter → Akkusativ *mein Gepäck* (no ending).

alternatives.de: Kann ich mein Gepäck hier lassen?
alternatives.en: Can I leave my luggage here?

alternatives.de: Kann ich meinen Koffer bis 15 Uhr bei Ihnen lassen?
alternatives.en: Can I leave my suitcase with you until 3 p.m.?

phrases.usage: A general complaint while you point at the thing; better name it: *Der Fernseher funktioniert nicht.* Staff usually answer *Ich schicke sofort jemanden.*
phrases.grammar: *es* refers to a neuter noun (*das Licht*) or to an unnamed thing. For a masculine or feminine noun, use *er* or *sie*: *Der Fernseher? Er funktioniert nicht.* *nicht* at the end negates the verb.

alternatives.en: That doesn't work.
The TV doesn't work.

phrases.usage: Report it to reception. *kaputt* is informal but completely normal in speech. The staff will send someone or offer another room.
phrases.grammar: *kaputt* is predicative after *sein*, so it has no ending. Before a noun it declines: *eine kaputte Heizung*. *die Heizung* is feminine (*-ung*).

alternatives.en: The heating isn't working.

alternatives.de: Im Zimmer ist es sehr kalt.
alternatives.en: It's very cold in the room.

phrases.usage: Report it to reception, for example in the morning before your shower. In Switzerland the spelling is *heisses*.
phrases.grammar: *es gibt* + Akkusativ. *kein* has no ending in the neuter Akkusativ, so the adjective shows the gender with the strong ending **-es**: kein heiß**es** Wasser.

alternatives.en: The water doesn't get warm.

alternatives.de: In der Dusche kommt nur kaltes Wasser.
alternatives.en: Only cold water comes out of the shower.

phrases.usage: Ask at reception or tell the cleaning staff. More polite: *Könnte ich noch zwei Handtücher bekommen?*
phrases.grammar: *mehr* never takes an ending. *das Handtuch* has the plural *die Handtücher* (Umlaut + *-er*); a plural after *mehr* has no article.

alternatives.de: Könnte ich noch zwei Handtücher bekommen?
alternatives.en: Could I get two more towels?

alternatives.de: Können Sie mir bitte frische Handtücher bringen?
alternatives.en: Could you bring me fresh towels, please?

phrases.usage: Ask at reception. The answer is *Gern. Für wann?* With *mir* it is clear that the taxi is for you: *Können Sie mir ein Taxi bestellen?*
phrases.grammar: Modal *können* first, infinitive *bestellen* at the end. *das Taxi* is neuter → Akkusativ *ein Taxi*. An optional Dativ (*mir*) names the person it is for.

alternatives.de: Könnten Sie mir bitte ein Taxi rufen?
alternatives.en: Could you call me a taxi, please?

alternatives.de: Ich brauche ein Taxi für 7 Uhr.
alternatives.en: I need a taxi for 7 o'clock.

phrases.de: Haben Sie noch ein Zimmer frei?
phrases.en: Do you still have a room available?
phrases.usage: Ask when you arrive without a booking. The answer is *Ja, für wie viele Nächte?* or *Leider sind wir ausgebucht.* ('fully booked').
phrases.grammar: *ein Zimmer* is the Akkusativ object of *haben*; *frei* stands at the end as a predicative complement and has no ending. *noch* means 'still'.

alternatives.de: Ist für heute Nacht noch ein Zimmer frei?
alternatives.en: Is there still a room free for tonight?

alternatives.de: Haben Sie für heute Nacht noch etwas frei?
alternatives.en: Do you have anything free for tonight?

phrases.usage: The answer to *Wie lange bleiben Sie?* or *Für wie viele Nächte?* You can also give the end date: *Wir bleiben bis Sonntag.*
phrases.grammar: A time span without a preposition is in the Akkusativ: *drei Nächte* (for masculine nouns you can see it: *einen Tag*). *die Nacht* has the plural *Nächte* with Umlaut.

alternatives.en: For three nights, please.
We're staying until Sunday.

phrases.de: Was kostet das Zimmer pro Nacht?
phrases.en: How much is the room per night?
phrases.usage: Ask before you decide. The answer is *140 Franken pro Nacht, mit Frühstück.* In many holiday places a small tourist tax (*Kurtaxe*) is added per person and night.
phrases.grammar: *das Zimmer* is the subject (Nominativ). *pro* is followed by a noun without article: *pro Nacht, pro Person*.

alternatives.en: How much is one night?
How much is a double room?

phrases.de: Ist das Frühstück im Preis inbegriffen?
phrases.en: Is breakfast included in the price?
phrases.usage: Ask when you book or check in. The answer is *Ja, das Frühstück ist inklusive.* or *Nein, das kostet 20 Franken extra.*
phrases.grammar: *inbegriffen* ('included') looks like a Partizip II, but it is used only as an adjective (the verb *inbegreifen* is no longer used). Here it is predicative, so it has no ending. *im Preis* = *in dem Preis*, Dativ (*der Preis*).

alternatives.en: Is breakfast included?
Does breakfast cost extra?

phrases.usage: The receptionist asks this at check-in. Show your passport or ID card and say *Ja, hier, bitte.* Hotels often also ask you to fill in a short form (*Meldeschein*).
phrases.grammar: *dürfen* asks for permission and sounds polite. *Ihren* is the possessive for *Sie* (always capitalised); *der Ausweis* is masculine → Akkusativ *Ihren*.

alternatives.en: Your passport, please.

alternatives.de: Kann ich bitte Ihren Ausweis sehen?
alternatives.en: Can I see your ID, please?

phrases.de: Kann ich ein ruhigeres Zimmer bekommen?
phrases.en: Can I get a quieter room?
phrases.usage: Ask when your room is next to a busy street or the lift. The receptionist checks and answers *Ich schaue, was ich machen kann.*
phrases.grammar: The comparative *ruhiger* still takes an adjective ending before a noun: after *ein* (neuter Akkusativ) → ein ruhiger**es** Zimmer. *bekommen* means 'to get', not 'to become' (false friend).

alternatives.de: Das Zimmer ist leider sehr laut.
alternatives.en: Unfortunately the room is very noisy.

alternatives.de: Haben Sie ein Zimmer zum Hof?
alternatives.en: Do you have a room facing the courtyard?
